exports.name: A2A_ACCESS_DENIED
exports.doc:
JSON-RPC error code (HTTP 403) of a message the caller may not send: `error.data.reason` says why (`ACCESS_DENIED`,
`UNKNOWN_SKILL`, `NO_RULE_FOR_CALLER`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`). Tasks of other callers answer A2A's own `-32001`.

exports.name: A2A_CONFIRMATION_REQUESTED
exports.doc:
JSON-RPC error code (HTTP 403) telling an agent that acts for a person that the person must confirm this request
first: a confirmation request was filed (`error.data.confirmationId`, `error.data.expiresAt`); retry once approved.

exports.name: agentAttestationUri
exports.doc: The URI of the attestation extension Better IAM adds to every card it signs.

exports.name: AgentCardError
exports.doc:
Why an agent card was refused by `verifyAgentCard` or `discoverAgent`: `reason` is `unsigned`, `untrusted-key`,
`signature`, `attestation`, `expired`, `issuer`, `tenant`, `endpoint`, `malformed` or `fetch`.

exports.name: createA2aAuthorizer
exports.doc: Decisions shared by the gate and by handlers written with an A2A SDK.

exports.name: createA2aGate
exports.doc:
The gate: `gate(request, next)` answers the request itself (the agent card, challenges, refusals) or passes it to
`next` (the A2A server's handler) with the authenticated caller, recording who started each task on the way back.

exports.name: createCardAttestor
exports.doc:
Keeps an agent's own card attested: returns a function that yields the signed card, signing on first use and again
when the attestation nears its end. Concurrent calls share one signing request; when re-signing fails while the
previous card is still valid, that card is returned.

exports.name: createDelegationTokenCache
exports.doc:
For the agent side: returns a function yielding a current delegation token for an audience (and scopes), issuing one
on first use and again when it nears its end, so an agent calling a service repeatedly does not ask for a token on
every call. Concurrent calls for the same audience share one request.

exports.name: DelegationTokenError
exports.doc:
Why `verifyDelegationToken` refused a token: `reason` is `malformed`, `type`, `issuer`, `untrusted-key`,
`signature`, `audience`, `tenant`, `expired`, `not-yet-valid`, `lifetime`, `replay` or `fetch`.

exports.name: discoverAgent
exports.doc:
Fetches a remote agent's card (`url` itself when it ends in `.json`, otherwise `/.well-known/agent-card.json` on its
origin) and verifies it with `verifyAgentCard`, requiring the card's `url` to be on the origin it was fetched from.
Call it only with agent addresses you chose: it makes an outbound request.

exports.name: handoffMetadataKey
exports.doc:
The A2A message metadata key that carries a Better IAM hand-off (`delegations.handoff`) from the calling agent to the
agent it calls, so the called agent can act for the same person with `delegations.assume`.

exports.name: handoffOf
exports.doc:
The hand-off an A2A request carries (the called side): the delegation id in the message's metadata, else in the
request's. Open a session for it with the called agent's own key (`delegations.assume`), which refuses hand-offs that
are not this agent's.

exports.name: memoryTaskOwners
exports.doc: In-memory owners: at most `maxTasks` entries (default 100000), each kept `ttlMs` (default seven days).

exports.name: taskOwnerOf
exports.doc: The owner key of a caller: the same person through the same agent (or none), or the same OAuth client and subject.

exports.name: verifyAgentCard
exports.doc:
Verifies that `card` was signed by a trusted Better IAM deployment and that its attestation is current: one of the
card's signatures verifies over the canonical card (RFC 8785, without `signatures`) with a trusted key, the card
carries exactly one attestation, it is neither expired nor from the future, and it matches `issuers`, `tenantId`
and `origin` when given. Throws `AgentCardError` otherwise.

exports.name: verifyDelegationToken
exports.doc:
Verifies a delegation token: a compact JWT of type `biam-delegation+jwt`, signed (EdDSA or ES256) by a key of the
trusted issuer it names, for exactly `audience` (and `tenantId`), current, and issued for at most an hour. Returns
who acts for whom; throws `DelegationTokenError` otherwise. Revocation reaches a token only when it expires, so keep
lifetimes short, or verify inside the deployment with `iam.a2a.verifyDelegationToken(token, { live: true })`.

exports.name: withHandoff
exports.doc: Adds a hand-off to an A2A message's metadata (the calling side).

exports.name: libsqlAdapter
exports.doc:
libSQL persistence: local files (including encrypted ones and embedded replicas) and remote Turso or sqld
databases through one adapter. Transactions serialize per database in this process and take the writer lock
(`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) before any read; remote servers queue write transactions themselves.

exports.name: postgresAdapter
exports.doc: Transactions serialize through a database advisory lock, including other adapter instances.

exports.name: sqliteAdapter
exports.doc:
SQLite serializes operations per canonical filename in this process. SQLite's
own BEGIN IMMEDIATE lock coordinates other processes with a bounded wait.
Use PostgreSQL when sustained concurrent writes or large datasets are expected.

exports.name: AuthService
exports.doc:
Authentication services. The class is assembled from feature modules (sessions, account management,
passwordless, MFA, passkeys) over a shared base. Low-level transaction helpers are for trusted server integrations only.

exports.name: characterClasses
exports.doc: Lowercase, uppercase, digit, and everything else.

exports.name: createMemoryRateLimiter
exports.doc:
In-process limiter for single-instance deployments and tests. Counters are not shared between processes, and the
map is bounded by `maxKeys`.

exports.name: createStoreRateLimiter
exports.doc: The default limiter: durable counters in the IAM database, committed independently so rejected credentials cannot roll back their attempt.

exports.name: credentialTokenKinds
exports.doc: The session kind each credential token type must resolve to; the stored kind stays authoritative.

exports.name: credentialTokenScanPattern
exports.doc:
A pattern secret scanners can use to find better-iam credential tokens in text. It needs lookbehind support; without
it, use `biam_(ses|key|rol|sts|dlg)_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{49}` with explicit boundary rules.

exports.name: decryptSecret
exports.doc: Opens a sealed value with the current secret or, during a rotation, a previous one.

exports.name: encryptSecret
exports.doc: Authenticated encryption; the application secret must be a high-entropy, stable secret.

exports.name: isCommonPassword
exports.doc: The built-in weak-password screen: common passwords, keyboard walks and sequences, and low variety.

exports.name: newCredentialToken
exports.doc:
A new opaque credential token, `biam_<type>_` + 43 random base64url characters + a 6-character CRC-32 checksum (58
characters in all). The checksum lets scanners and the server reject garbage early; it authenticates nothing.

exports.name: openSecret
exports.doc:
Opens a sealed value with the first of `secrets` that authenticates it, and says which one
(0 is the current secret; higher indexes are previous ones kept during a rotation). Undefined
when none does.

exports.name: parseCredentialToken
exports.doc:
Parses a prefixed credential token: its type when the shape and checksum match, otherwise undefined. The type is a
routing hint only; authorization always uses the stored session.

exports.name: pwnedPasswords
exports.doc:
A Have I Been Pwned "range" client (k-anonymity): hashes the password with SHA-1, sends only the first five hex
characters, and matches the returned suffixes locally. Network failures accept the password unless `failClosed`.

exports.name: renderDeliveryMessage
exports.doc:
Renders the messages Better IAM queues (`verify-email`, `password-reset`, `email-change`, `magic-link`, `code`,
`mfa-code`, `new-sign-in`, `sign-in-failures`, `certification-review`, `certification-reminder`, `delegation-request`,
`delegation-confirmation`, `team-join-request`, `team-join-decided`, `team-review-requested`, `spend-alert`,
`spend-anomaly`, `billing-statement`, `payment-reminder`,
`owner-invitation`, `member-invitation`)
into a subject, plain text, and HTML, so a
delivery callback can hand them to any provider. Returns undefined for templates it does not know (plugins,
newer features), which the callback should render itself.

exports.name: renderDeliveryMessage
exports.doc:
Renders the messages Better IAM queues (`verify-email`, `password-reset`, `email-change`, `magic-link`, `code`,
`mfa-code`, `new-sign-in`, `sign-in-failures`, `certification-review`, `certification-reminder`, `delegation-request`,
`delegation-confirmation`, `team-join-request`, `team-join-decided`, `team-review-requested`, `spend-alert`,
`spend-anomaly`, `billing-statement`, `payment-reminder`,
`owner-invitation`, `member-invitation`)
into a subject, plain text, and HTML, so a
delivery callback can hand them to any provider. Returns undefined for templates it does not know (plugins,
newer features), which the callback should render itself.

exports.name: builtinCommands
exports.doc: Every built-in command, in help order.

exports.name: CliError
exports.doc:
A command-line failure: an `IamError` (same `code` contract) that may carry a hint, printed on its own line by
the `better-iam` binary, telling the person what to run or set next.

exports.name: cliManifest
exports.doc: The machine-readable description of every built-in command (what `better-iam help --json` prints), for docs and tools.

exports.name: commandHelp
exports.doc: `better-iam help <command>`: usage, description, arguments, flags, and examples.

exports.name: configFileNames
exports.doc: Configuration file names the CLI looks for, in this order, in the working directory and then each parent.

exports.name: configFromEnv
exports.doc:
Deployment options from environment variables alone (twelve-factor style), for containers and CI jobs that have
no configuration file:

- `BETTER_IAM_DATABASE_URL` (required): `postgres://…`, `sqlite:./iam.db` (or a path ending in `.db`), or
  `libsql://…` / `file:…` (needs `@better-iam/adapter-libsql` installed; `BETTER_IAM_DATABASE_TOKEN` authenticates)
- `BETTER_IAM_SECRET` (required), `BETTER_IAM_PREVIOUS_SECRETS` (comma-separated, during a rotation)
- `BETTER_IAM_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:3000`), `BETTER_IAM_BASE_PATH`, `BETTER_IAM_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`

Everything else keeps its default; spread the result and add callbacks (email, resolvers) in code when you need
them: `betterIam({ ...(await configFromEnv()), authentication: { sendEmail } })`.

exports.name: createCli
exports.doc:
Creates a `better-iam`-style program from code: the built-in commands plus your own (`defineCommand`), with the same
parsing, help, configuration loading, and output. Use it to ship a project CLI, or to run commands in tests.

exports.name: createProfileStore
exports.doc:
Opens the saved-session file that `login`, `logout`, `profiles`, and token commands use, located from `env` (see
`credentialsPath`), so tools can list, save, or switch profiles the same way the CLI does.

exports.name: credentialsPath
exports.doc:
Where saved sessions live: `BETTER_IAM_CREDENTIALS`, else `%APPDATA%\better-iam\credentials.json` on Windows, else
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/better-iam/credentials.json` or `~/.config/better-iam/credentials.json`. Read only from the
given environment, so an embedding program (and every test) decides whether a profile can be found at all.

exports.name: defineCommand
exports.doc:
Declares a CLI command with typed flags. Export an array of them as `commands` from `better-iam.config.mjs` to add
project commands (seeding, reports, migrations of your own) that get the same flag parsing, help, configuration
loading, and output formatting as the built-in ones.

```js
export const commands = [
  defineCommand({
    name: 'seed',
    summary: 'Create the demo organization',
    target: 'config',
    flags: { slug: { type: 'string', description: 'Organization slug', default: 'demo' } },
    async run({ iam, flags }) { const instance = await iam(); ... return { created: true }; },
  }),
];
```

exports.name: findConfigFile
exports.doc: The nearest configuration file in `cwd` or one of its parents, like Prettier and ESLint find theirs.

exports.name: formatResult
exports.doc: Turns a command result into the text printed on stdout. Strings are printed as they are.

exports.name: lintTenantConfig
exports.doc: Offline checks: the shape (`validateTenantConfig`) plus cross-references between the file's own items.

exports.name: listRoutes
exports.doc: Every route the HTTP API serves for an instance, with whether it needs a credential.

exports.name: loadConfig
exports.doc:
Loads a configuration file and creates its instance: the same resolution the CLI uses, for scripts, workers, and
tests that want `better-iam.config.mjs` without the command line. Close `instance.store` when done.

exports.name: loadTenantConfig
exports.doc:
Reads a desired tenant configuration for `config-plan` / `config-apply` / `config-validate`: a `.json` file, or a
JavaScript/TypeScript module whose default export is the configuration or a (possibly async) factory of it. Modules
let one file compute per-environment values (`env.STAGE === 'prod' ? ... : ...`) and share constants with the app.

exports.name: localTransport
exports.doc:
Calls API routes in process on a configured instance, as `token` (or with no credential), exposing exactly the
routes and credential rules of the HTTP handler; what token commands use without `--url`.

exports.name: main
exports.doc:
Runs the CLI like the `better-iam` binary: prints `CODE: message` (and a hint) on failure and resolves with the exit
status, 0 on success, 2 for a usage mistake, 1 otherwise. For wrappers that ship their own binary.

exports.name: processIO
exports.doc: The process's own IO: stdout, stderr, `process.env`, and prompts when both stdin and stderr are terminals.

exports.name: remoteTransport
exports.doc:
Calls API routes on a running IAM server over HTTP(S) with a bearer token, through the typed client (request IDs,
one retry after a short rate limit); what token commands use with `--url` or a profile saved against a server.

exports.name: runBinary
exports.doc:
What the `better-iam` binary does: runs `main()` on the process arguments, sets the exit status, and fails a command
that can never finish instead of exiting 0. For packages that ship the CLI under their own `bin`.

exports.name: runCli
exports.doc:
Runs one `better-iam` command line (without the program name) and resolves when it finishes; failures reject with an
`IamError` (or `CliError`) whose `code` says what went wrong. This command loads trusted application configuration
as executable JavaScript.

exports.name: selectPath
exports.doc:
Selects part of a result for `--query`: dotted keys (`summary.create`), array indexes (`roles.0` or `roles[0]`),
and `[]` to map over an array (`findings[].kind`). A missing key selects `null` rather than failing, like `jq`.

exports.name: usageError
exports.doc: A usage mistake (unknown flag, missing value, bad number): the binary exits with status 2 for these.

exports.name: ClientError
exports.doc: HTTP errors preserve the server's stable code without exposing raw response bodies.

exports.name: createIamClient
IamClientError
exports.doc: HTTP errors preserve the server's stable code without exposing raw response bodies.

exports.name: browserSupportsWebAuthn
exports.doc: Determine if the browser is capable of Webauthn

exports.name: browserSupportsWebAuthnAutofill
exports.doc:
Determine if the browser supports conditional UI, so that WebAuthn credentials can
be shown to the user in the browser's typical password autofill popup.

exports.name: platformAuthenticatorIsAvailable
exports.doc:
Determine whether the browser can communicate with a built-in authenticator, like
Touch ID, Android fingerprint scanner, or Windows Hello.

This method will _not_ be able to tell you the name of the platform authenticator.

exports.name: startAuthentication
exports.doc: Begin authenticator "login" via WebAuthn assertion

exports.name: startRegistration
exports.doc: Begin authenticator "registration" via WebAuthn attestation

exports.name: WebAuthnAbortService
exports.doc:
A service singleton to help ensure that only a single WebAuthn ceremony is active at a time.

Users of **@simplewebauthn/browser** shouldn't typically need to use this, but it can help e.g.
developers building projects that use client-side routing to better control the behavior of
their UX in response to router navigation events.

exports.name: createSessionStore
exports.doc:
Framework-agnostic session state. The React and Vue bindings subscribe to it;
it can also drive other frameworks or plain scripts.

exports.name: isUnauthenticated
exports.doc: The server answers 401/403 for missing, expired, or step-up-required credentials; anything else is a transport failure.

exports.name: appendAuditEvent
exports.doc: Records an audit event at the end of its tenant's chain. Every audit insert must go through here.

exports.name: applyMigrations
exports.doc:
Creates the schema and applies missing named migrations, recording each in `iam_migrations`.
Run it inside the adapter's serialized write transaction. Returns the names applied now.

exports.name: auditEventHash
exports.doc: The hash of an event: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of every field except `hash` itself.

exports.name: auditGenesis
exports.doc: The `previousHash` of the first event of every chain.

exports.name: authMethods
exports.doc: The sign-in methods a tenant policy can allow or restrict; impersonation is an administrative action, not a sign-in.

exports.name: canonicalizeJson
exports.doc:
The JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785): the single serialization of a JSON value that signers and verifiers
agree on. Object members are sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names at every depth, numbers use the
ECMAScript shortest form and strings the escaping of `JSON.stringify`, and there is no whitespace. Unlike
`canonicalJson`, member order does not depend on how a JavaScript engine orders integer-like keys.

Members whose value is `undefined`, a function or a symbol are left out and such array entries become `null`, as
`JSON.stringify` does; `toJSON` is honoured. Throws a `TypeError` for values JSON cannot represent: non-finite
numbers, bigints, cycles, and a top-level value without a JSON form.

exports.name: canonicalJson
exports.doc: Deterministic JSON: object keys sorted recursively, `undefined` properties omitted, arrays kept in order.

exports.name: chainAuditEvent
exports.doc:
Assigns the next chain position to an event and advances the tenant's chain head. The caller stores the returned
event; `appendAuditEvent` does both. Must run inside the transaction that records the event.

exports.name: COLLECTIONS_SQL
exports.doc: Distinct collection names in the records table.

exports.name: compareIds
exports.doc: Code-point (UTF-8 byte) order, the order of SQLite's BINARY and PostgreSQL's "C" collation.

exports.name: copyStore
exports.doc:
Copies every record from `source` into an empty, migrated `target` (for example SQLite to
PostgreSQL). Reads in one source transaction and writes in one target transaction, so the copy
is consistent and all-or-nothing.

exports.name: decodeJsonbDocument
exports.doc: The original record JSON of a document written by `encodeJsonbDocument`.

exports.name: definePolicy
exports.doc: Typed document builder. Returns a detached document after runtime validation.

exports.name: delegationActor
exports.doc: The `act` claim for a chain of agents, the person's own delegate first and the agent acting now last.

exports.name: delegationTokenLimits
exports.doc: Lifetimes (seconds) and the longest chain of actors a delegation token carries.

exports.name: delegationTokenScopePattern
exports.doc: One scope a delegation token may carry: an action, or an action pattern whose only wildcard is `*`.

exports.name: delegationTokenType
exports.doc: The JWT `typ` header of delegation tokens: verifiers refuse any other.

exports.name: describeRecords
exports.doc:
The adapter-independent part of `IamStore.describe()`: schema version, applied migrations, and
record counts per collection. Missing tables read as empty, so an unmigrated database reports
empty lists; any other failure rejects. Run it outside a transaction on PostgreSQL (a failed
statement would abort the transaction).

exports.name: encodeJsonbDocument
exports.doc: Record JSON as the PostgreSQL adapter stores it: valid jsonb, reversible by `decodeJsonbDocument`.

exports.name: encodeLegacyPostgresRows
exports.doc:
Migration hook for PostgreSQL: rewrites rows written before the value encoding existed, whose
text jsonb would reject, so the jsonb index of `0002_query_indexes` can be built.

exports.name: evaluatePolicy
exports.doc:
Grants form a union; every boundary is an independent intersection. A boundary
never grants access. Callers must establish trusted context and tenant scope.

exports.name: EXPIRY_FIELDS
exports.doc:
Numeric fields SQL adapters index for `findOrdered` across a whole collection, so retention
sweeps find expired and long-delivered records without scanning (`0004_expiry_indexes`).

exports.name: exportStore
exports.doc:
Writes a snapshot through `write`, one line at a time (without newlines). Runs in one store
transaction, so the snapshot is consistent; that also holds the store's write lock until done.

exports.name: findOrdered
exports.doc:
Records matching `filter` whose numeric `order.field` lies in `[from, to]`, ordered by that field
(ties by id, ascending) and paged. Uses the store's `findOrdered` when it has one and otherwise
orders a plain `find` in memory. `where` adds an in-memory predicate (for example a glob); the
store is then read in ordered chunks until the page is full, so it never loads everything.

exports.name: importStore
exports.doc:
Loads a snapshot into an empty, migrated store in one transaction: a malformed line, a record
the store refuses, or a missing or mismatched trailer rolls everything back.

exports.name: INDEXED_FIELDS
exports.doc:
High-cardinality string fields looked up across tenants or inside large collections (sessions,
identities, memberships, bindings, protocol artifacts, delivery queues). SQL adapters may index
them; the list only affects performance, never results. Every index adds work to each write, so
keep it to fields on hot or unscoped lookup paths.

exports.name: instrumentStore
exports.doc:
Wraps a store so every data call is reported to `onCall` (reads, writes, `collections`, and
`describe`; `transaction`, `migrate`, and `close` pass straight through), for slow-query logging, capacity planning,
and tests that bound how much work an operation does. The wrapper adds no behavior: results,
errors, and transactions are the underlying store's. `onCall` runs synchronously after each
call; exceptions it throws are ignored.

exports.name: ipCounterKey
exports.doc:
The key a per-address counter uses for a client: an IPv4 address as itself (the IPv4-mapped IPv6 form folded to
it), an IPv6 address as its /64 (`2001:db8:1:2::/64`), since one subscriber or host normally controls a whole
/64 and can rotate through it at will. Spelling variants of one address (case, zero compression) share a key.
Undefined when the value is not an IP address.

exports.name: ipMatches
exports.doc:
True when `address` lies inside `network` (an address or CIDR block of the same family). An IPv4-mapped IPv6
address (`::ffff:198.51.100.7`) matches the IPv4 networks that contain its IPv4 address, and an IPv4 address the
IPv4-mapped networks (`::ffff:198.51.100.0/120`) that contain it.

exports.name: isIpRange
exports.doc: True for an IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR block, as accepted by the `IpAddress` operator.

exports.name: isMissingTable
exports.doc: A query failed because a table does not exist (PostgreSQL 42P01, SQLite "no such table").

exports.name: JSONB_ESCAPE_KEY
exports.doc:
Reserved object key of the PostgreSQL value encoding (`encodeJsonbDocument`), which stores
strings jsonb cannot hold. Filters whose objects use it are evaluated in memory.

exports.name: LOOKUP_INDEX_STEPS
exports.doc:
The lookup fields each schema step indexes (SQLite and libSQL; PostgreSQL's document index covers
every field). A released step never changes: new fields get a new step.

exports.name: matchesFilter
exports.doc: The in-memory definition of filter semantics. Drivers' SQL must agree with it.

exports.name: matchPattern
exports.doc: Glob matching is anchored; only * and ? are operators. No regular expressions are accepted. Variables resolve from context.

exports.name: MAX_QUERY_CONDITIONS
exports.doc: Most typed conditions `planQuery` hands to a driver; further keys are filtered in memory.

exports.name: ORDERED_FIELDS
exports.doc: Numeric fields SQL adapters index for `findOrdered` within a tenant (audit time and sequence).

exports.name: planQuery
exports.doc: Splits a validated filter into driver conditions and keys left to the in-memory filter.

exports.name: postgresSelect
exports.doc: SELECT for PostgreSQL. Scalar tests share one jsonb containment test, served by a GIN index.

exports.name: QUERYABLE_FIELD
exports.doc: Field names a driver may inline into SQL paths. Other names are filtered in memory.

exports.name: readDelegationTokenClaims
exports.doc:
Checks the claims of a (signature-verified) delegation token against what the verifier expects: well formed, from an
accepted issuer, for exactly this audience (and tenant), current within the clock tolerance, and issued for at most
`delegationTokenLimits.maxSeconds`.

exports.name: RecordStore
exports.doc: Shared strict JSON behavior keeps SQLite, libSQL, and PostgreSQL semantically identical.

exports.name: resolvePolicyValue
exports.doc: Resolves the variables of a string condition value. Returns undefined when any variable is unresolved.

exports.name: schemaMigrations
exports.doc:
Ordered, append-only schema steps. Never edit a released step; add a new one.

Secondary indexes end in `id` so one index both finds rows and yields them in `ORDER BY id`
order. Without that, SQLite (which has no statistics until ANALYZE) prefers walking the
primary key in id order over an index lookup followed by a sort.

exports.name: SNAPSHOT_FORMAT
exports.doc:
Portable store snapshots: every record of every collection as JSON Lines, independent of the
adapter, for backups, moving from SQLite to PostgreSQL, and test fixtures. Records are copied
verbatim, so audit hash chains, token hashes, and encrypted secrets stay valid. A snapshot holds
credential hashes and encrypted secrets: protect it like the database itself.

Format: a header line `{ format, version, createdAt, collections }`, one `{ c, r }` line per
record (collection, record), and a trailer `{ end: true, records, collections }` with counts,
so a truncated file is detected before anything is committed.

exports.name: sqliteSelect
exports.doc: SELECT for SQLite and libSQL (JSON1). `json` conditions are not supported.

exports.name: storableString
exports.doc:
True when the string has no U+0000 and no unpaired surrogate. Such strings can be stored as
record values, but database text comparisons cannot represent them, so `find` evaluates filters
holding them in memory. Identifiers must satisfy it.

exports.name: storageError
exports.doc: Map database failures without leaking SQL or credential-bearing record data.

exports.name: summarizeStoreCalls
exports.doc: Totals of a list of calls, grouped by method and collection (`find:sessions`).

exports.name: tenantTreeActive
exports.doc: Walks a tenant and its ancestors: true only when every one exists and is active. Cycles read as inactive.

exports.name: validatePolicy
exports.doc: Validate untrusted documents before storage and again before evaluation.

exports.name: validPolicyVariables
exports.doc: Every `${...}` in a value must be a well-formed variable reference.

exports.name: verifyAuditChain
exports.doc:
Verifies a run of events from one tenant: contiguous sequences, each `previousHash` equal to the previous event's
hash (or `previousHash` of the first event when the run starts mid-chain), and every hash recomputable.
Events are sorted by sequence first, so exports and database reads can be passed as they come.

exports.name: adapterConformanceCases
exports.doc: A fresh copy of every conformance case, in a stable order.

exports.name: runAdapterConformance
exports.doc: Runs every case against fresh stores and collects failures instead of stopping at the first.

exports.name: createMcpAuthorizer
exports.doc: Decisions shared by the gate and by tool handlers written with an MCP SDK.

exports.name: createMcpGate
exports.doc:
The gate: `gate(request, next)` answers the request itself (metadata, challenges, refused calls) or passes it to
`next` (the MCP server's handler) with the authenticated caller, filtering `tools/list` answers on the way back.

exports.name: protectedResourceMetadataUrl
exports.doc: Where RFC 9728 metadata lives for a resource: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` + the resource path.

exports.name: checkRequestOrigin
exports.doc:
The CSRF boundary for application routes: a state-changing request authenticated by the session cookie (no
`Authorization` header) must come from this application's origin, the IAM origin, or a trusted origin. Session
cookies are `SameSite=Lax`, which still sends them from sibling subdomains, so the Origin check matters.
Returns the refusal, or null when the request may proceed.

inner session record. Impersonated sessions always fail a recency requirement, as the server's own check does.

Drops items the caller may not perform `action` on from a list response, using the reverse query `listAccessible`
over the registered resources of a managed type (one query per page of 1000, never one decision per item, so the

Subscribes every `@OnIamEvent` provider method to the IAM event stream at bootstrap and, when

exports.name: IamExceptionFilter
exports.doc:
Renders `IamError`s thrown from handlers and providers (for example `IamService.require` or direct `iam.api.*`

exports.name: IamGuard
exports.doc:
Authenticates every request it guards and enforces the handler's metadata: `@Public()`, `@Credentials()`,
`@RequireMfa()`, and `@Authorize()` rules. Failures render as the IAM server's `{ error: { code, message } }` body
with its status (401 unauthenticated, 403 denied, 429 rate limited).

exports.name: IamHttpMiddleware
exports.doc: Nest middleware form of `createIamRequestHandler`, registered by `IamModule.forRoot({ mount: true })`.

exports.name: IamModule
exports.doc:

globally, mounts the IAM HTTP API, and binds `@OnIamEvent` handlers.

An OpenID Shared Signals Framework transmitter: turns IAM audit events (sessions revoked, credentials changed,

exports.name: createProjectsPlugin

Registering the plugin adds the `projects:read` and `projects:write` actions
to the catalog and mounts `POST /api/iam/plugins/projects/{create|list|get|update|archive|restore}`.

exports.name: useAgreements

exports.name: useAuthorize
exports.doc:
Batched advisory decisions for rendering menus and buttons. Re-evaluated when the checks or the signed-in identity change;

exports.name: useConfirmations

(`billing.check`), to warn before a costly action. `allowed` is `true` until the answer arrives; the server still
refuses usage recorded with `enforceBudgets`.

exports.name: useTeams

Outbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning: keeps downstream applications' user directories in step with a tenant's members.

Composes the IAM server: configuration and catalog validation, the authentication service, the shared context,
the service modules, the provisioning API, deployment helpers, federation callbacks, and the HTTP transports.

exports.name: createInferenceGateway

exports.name: createJsonlAuditArchive
exports.doc:
A file sink for `auditArchive`: one JSON Lines file per batch at
`{directory}/{tenantId}/{fromSequence}-{toSequence}.jsonl` (sequences zero-padded, so files sort
in chain order). Files are write-once: each is written under a unique temporary name, flushed,
and published with a hard link that never replaces an existing file. Writing the same batch
again is accepted; a different batch under an existing name is refused (`ARCHIVE_CONFLICT`), so
a restored or tampered database can never overwrite archived events. After a crash, files can
overlap; read events by `sequence`.

exports.doc:
Creates an offline verifier for IAM session JWTs. It enforces the `biam-session+jwt` type, the EdDSA/ES256
allowlist (pinned to each key's `alg` for a local key set), the exact issuer, one of the configured audiences,
`exp`/`nbf` with clock tolerance, the lifetime cap, the accepted kinds and the claim types.

exports.name: dayOf
exports.doc: The local day `YYYY-MM-DD` an instant falls on.

exports.name: defineConfig
defineTenantConfig
exports.doc:
Types a tenant's configuration as code (roles, policies, groups, bindings, packages, invariants, agreements) for
`better-iam config-plan|config-apply --input tenant.config.ts`, or a factory that computes it per tenant and
environment. Returns its argument unchanged; `iam.api.config.apply(credential, { tenantId, config })` applies the
same value from code.

exports.name: delegationTokenLimits
exports.doc: Lifetimes (seconds) and the longest chain of actors a delegation token carries.

exports.name: delegationTokenType
exports.doc: The JWT `typ` header of delegation tokens: verifiers refuse any other.

exports.name: departmentHeads
exports.doc:
The heads of a department (identity IDs): its own head and, with `includeAncestors`, the heads of the departments
above it, nearest first and without duplicates.

exports.name: departmentOf
exports.doc: The ID of the department a person belongs to, if any.

exports.name: departmentPath
exports.doc: Department IDs from the top of the tree down to `departmentId` itself (for roll-ups); empty when unknown.

exports.name: inferenceResourceType
exports.doc: The resource type and action the inference module adds to the permission catalog.

exports.name: inferenceToolAction
exports.doc: The action decided on each `model-tool/{kind}` a request asks for, for models whose `providerTools` is `policy`.

exports.name: inferenceToolResourceType
exports.doc:
Tools the provider runs itself (web search, code execution, remote MCP servers, ...), as resources of this type named
by kind (`model-tool/web_search`, `model-tool/mcp:{host}`), checked with `inference:use-tool` for models whose
`providerTools` is `policy`.

exports.name: isTeamMaintainer
exports.doc:
Whether a person maintains a team: a live maintainer membership of the team itself or, with `includeAncestors`, of
any team above it (a parent team's maintainers manage its child teams too).

exports.name: lintPolicy
exports.doc:
Lints a policy document: validates it as storage would, then reports statements that grant more than intended,
conditions that can never match or silently fail open, and statements that are shadowed or duplicated. The
context tells the linter which identity attributes, resource attributes, and application keys exist. Pattern
comparisons are budgeted: past the budget, a `shadowed-allow-skipped` note replaces the rest of the shadow check.

exports.name: looksLikeJwt
exports.doc: True for a compact JWS shape (three base64url segments); says nothing about validity.

exports.name: machineIdentity
exports.doc: Machine accounts: service accounts and agents. They hold API keys and never sign in.

exports.name: nextWatermark
exports.doc:
The next `sessionsRevokedBefore` for a record: `max(current ?? 0, before ?? now + 1)`, so a watermark only ever
moves forward and never lies in the future (it can neither resurrect a session nor block new issuance). The default
revokes every session issued so far. Throws INVALID_INPUT when `before` is not a safe integer >= 0 or is > now + 1.

exports.name: periodBounds
exports.doc: The first instant of a period and of the next one.

exports.name: periodOf
exports.doc: The billing period an instant falls in.

exports.name: priceBreakdown
exports.doc:
How a quantity is priced, tier by tier, for invoice sub-lines: the tiers used, the free units, and what the tiers
came to before the price's minimum or maximum.

exports.name: priceQuantity
exports.doc: The amount, in micros, a period's quantity costs under a price: its tiers, then its minimum and maximum.

exports.name: priceSpec
exports.doc:
Validates a price given in currency units (`unitAmount`, `tiers[].unitAmount` / `flatAmount`, `packageAmount`) and
returns it in micros. Tiers ascend by `upTo`, and the last one has `upTo: null`.

exports.name: primaryTeamOf
exports.doc: The person's oldest live direct team membership, for callers that attribute to one team only.

exports.name: providerToolsOf
exports.doc:
The tools a request asks the provider to run (or that the provider defines for the model to drive): Anthropic
server and Anthropic-defined tools (`tools[].type` other than `custom`) and remote MCP servers (`mcp_servers`); OpenAI
Responses built-in tools (`tools[].type` other than `function` and `custom`, MCP servers as `mcp:{host}` or
`mcp:{connector_id}`), and a stored prompt (`prompt`, which may bring tools of its own); Chat Completions web search
(`web_search_options`). Functions the caller runs itself are not listed. At most 65 entries are returned (more are
refused), from the first 256 tools and 64 MCP servers (the gateway refuses requests with more).

exports.name: publicOidcProvider
exports.doc:
An OIDC provider as the API returns it: an explicit allowlist projection (static keys are public members only,
as validated when they were stored).

exports.name: publicTrust
exports.doc:
A trust as the API returns it: an allowlist projection that never carries the external ID hash, reports whether an
external ID is required, and reads legacy records (no kind) as identity trusts.

exports.name: readDelegationTokenClaims
exports.doc:
Checks the claims of a (signature-verified) delegation token against what the verifier expects: well formed, from an
accepted issuer, for exactly this audience (and tenant), current within the clock tolerance, and issued for at most
`delegationTokenLimits.maxSeconds`.

exports.name: renderInvoiceHtml
exports.doc:
The invoice as a standalone HTML page (print it or save it as PDF): issuer, bill-to, number and dates, lines with
tier sub-lines and service periods, discounts, commitment, credit, tax, payments, credit notes, and amount due.

exports.name: revokedByWatermark
exports.doc:
Whether a session issued at `createdAt` falls under any revocation watermark (`sessionsRevokedBefore` of its role,
trust or provider): true when it was created strictly before a numeric watermark. Missing watermarks are ignored.

exports.name: rolloutBucket
exports.doc:
The rollout position (0 to 99.99) of a tenant branch for a flag: stable per key and tenant, so raising the
percentage only ever adds tenants, and different flags spread over different tenants.

exports.name: SESSION_TOKEN_ALGORITHMS
exports.doc: The only signature algorithms IAM issues or accepts for session JWTs.

exports.name: SESSION_TOKEN_TYPE
exports.doc: The `typ` header of every IAM session JWT; other token classes (assertions, OAuth `at+jwt`) never carry it.

exports.name: SessionTokenError
exports.doc: Every verification failure. `reason` is for logs and metrics; clients should only see the 401.

exports.name: shiftPeriod
exports.doc: A period `months` after (or before, when negative) another.

exports.name: teamMaintainers
exports.doc: The live direct maintainers of a team (identity IDs, oldest first).

exports.name: teamsOf
exports.doc:
The teams a person belongs to at `at` (default now): their live direct memberships (oldest first) and, with
`includeAncestors`, the parent teams those memberships make them part of. Team IDs, never backing group IDs.
There is no membership history, so callers that attribute something to teams should call this when it happens.

exports.name: temporarySessionKinds
exports.doc: The temporary kinds: derived from a source credential, bounded by it, and never usable for self-service.

exports.name: usageCost
exports.doc: Cost of a call in micro-dollars: tokens × dollars per million tokens (cached input at its own price when set).

exports.name: usageFrom
exports.doc:
Token counts from a provider's usage object (Anthropic, OpenAI Chat Completions / Embeddings, or OpenAI Responses);
undefined when there is none. Cached input tokens are counted apart from other input.

exports.name: validateTenantConfig
exports.doc: Validates the shape of a desired configuration; references are checked against the tenant during planning.

exports.name: verifyAssertion
exports.doc:
Verifies an assertion against the derived key, audience, optional issuer, and time; returns its
claims. `key` may list several keys (`iam.assertionKeys()`) while a deployment secret rotates.

exports.name: verifyAuditChain
exports.doc:
Verifies a run of events from one tenant: contiguous sequences, each `previousHash` equal to the previous event's
hash (or `previousHash` of the first event when the run starts mid-chain), and every hash recomputable.
Events are sorted by sequence first, so exports and database reads can be passed as they come.

exports.name: verifyWebhookSignature
exports.doc: Verifies a webhook signature produced by Better IAM. `signature` is the X-Better-IAM-Signature header value.

exports.name: webTrustTagClaims
exports.doc:
A web-identity trust's claim-to-tag mapping: at most 10 entries, each a session tag key (unique case-insensitively)
mapped to a flattened claim name (`token.<claim>`).

exports.name: WrongRegionError
exports.doc:
The organization is served by another region's deployment. `location` is its sign-in URL there (when one can be
built), so a sign-in page can redirect instead of showing an error. Answered with HTTP 421 Misdirected Request.

exports.name: assertionKey
exports.doc: The verification key for a deployment secret: SHA-256 of a purpose-bound derivation, as hex.

exports.name: verifyAssertion
exports.doc:
Verifies an assertion against the derived key, audience, optional issuer, and time; returns its
claims. `key` may list several keys (`iam.assertionKeys()`) while a deployment secret rotates.

exports.name: createSessionTokenVerifier
exports.doc:
Creates an offline verifier for IAM session JWTs. It enforces the `biam-session+jwt` type, the EdDSA/ES256
allowlist (pinned to each key's `alg` for a local key set), the exact issuer, one of the configured audiences,
`exp`/`nbf` with clock tolerance, the lifetime cap, the accepted kinds and the claim types.

exports.name: looksLikeJwt
exports.doc: True for a compact JWS shape (three base64url segments); says nothing about validity.

exports.name: MAX_SESSION_TOKEN_LENGTH
exports.doc: Longest accepted compact serialization, in characters.

exports.name: SESSION_TOKEN_ALGORITHMS
exports.doc: The only signature algorithms IAM issues or accepts for session JWTs.

exports.name: SESSION_TOKEN_TYPE
exports.doc: The `typ` header of every IAM session JWT; other token classes (assertions, OAuth `at+jwt`) never carry it.

exports.name: SessionTokenError
exports.doc: Every verification failure. `reason` is for logs and metrics; clients should only see the 401.

exports.name: createIam
createSessionStore
exports.doc:
Framework-agnostic session state. The React and Vue bindings subscribe to it;
it can also drive other frameworks or plain scripts.

exports.name: getIamContext
exports.doc: The `Iam` a parent shared with `setIamContext`.

exports.name: isUnauthenticated
exports.doc: The server answers 401/403 for missing, expired, or step-up-required credentials; anything else is a transport failure.

exports.name: setIamContext
exports.doc: Shares an `Iam` with descendant components; call during component initialisation.

exports.name: checkStepUp
exports.doc:
Checks a session against a step-up requirement; null when it qualifies. Accepts the `getSession` result or its
inner session record. Impersonated sessions always fail a recency requirement, as the server's own check does.

exports.name: createIamKit
isAuthenticationError
exports.doc: True for the errors `getSession` raises when there is no usable session.

exports.name: isKitControlError
exports.doc: True for SvelteKit's own control-flow throws (`redirect()`, `error()`), which must propagate untouched.

exports.name: parseSetCookie
exports.doc: Parses one `Set-Cookie` header into the name, decoded value, and options `event.cookies.set` accepts.

exports.name: safeRedirectPath
exports.doc: A same-site relative path safe to redirect to, or `fallback`. Refuses schemes, `//host`, and backslash tricks.

exports.name: createHydration
exports.doc: A plain object hydration store; serialize `state` into the page and pass the parsed object back on the client.

exports.name: createIam
exports.doc: The Vue plugin: one typed client and one session store for the app. `app.use(createIam({ client }))`.

exports.name: createSessionStore
exports.doc:
Framework-agnostic session state. The React and Vue bindings subscribe to it;
it can also drive other frameworks or plain scripts.

exports.name: IamCan
exports.doc:
Renders the default slot only when the advisory decision allows the action, the `fallback` slot otherwise, and the
`loading` slot meanwhile. `<IamCan tenant-id="t1" action="projects:delete" :resource="{ type: 'project', id }">`.

exports.name: isUnauthenticated
exports.doc: The server answers 401/403 for missing, expired, or step-up-required credentials; anything else is a transport failure.

exports.name: useAccessible
exports.doc: The registered resources of a managed type the signed-in principal may act on; refetched when the input or identity changes.

exports.name: useAccessPaths
exports.doc: Whether the signed-in person may perform an action and, if not, the self-service paths that would allow it.

exports.name: useAgreements
exports.doc: The signed-in person's terms of use and a way to accept them; policies can hold back access until they do.

exports.name: useAuthorize
exports.doc:
Batched advisory decisions for rendering menus and buttons. Accepts a ref or getter so the checks can follow reactive
state; the server still enforces every operation.

exports.name: useCan
exports.doc: One advisory decision as a boolean ref, false while loading or signed out.

exports.name: useIamClient
exports.doc: The client passed to `createIam`, typed as the caller declares it.

exports.name: useSession
exports.doc: Reactive session state plus refresh, sign-out, and manual replacement.

exports.name: useTeams
exports.doc: The signed-in person's teams with self-service joining and leaving (`teams.listMine`, `requestToJoin`, `leave`).
